newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan FTC wants NTT to cut cell phone unit stake.
newsitem.headline: Japan FTC wants NTT to cut cell phone unit stake.

text.p: Japan's Fair Trade Commission said on Friday it would like Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to reduce its stake in its cellular phone unit to 30 percent or less from the current 95 percent.
The anti-monopoly watchdog wants the cut to take place when the cellular phone unit, NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc (NTT DoCoMo), goes public, an FTC official said.

"We want to see the parent NTT, which virtually dominates Japan's regional call networks, and the cell phone unit, which uses NTT's regional networks, clearly separated from a competitive viewpoint," the official said.
"It would be perfect if NTT were to cut its stake to less than 10 percent. We hope to see it down to at least 20 to 30 percent," she said.
But an NTT spokesman earlier told Reuters the company believes that legally it does not have to reduce its stake, and it wants to maintain a majority stake in the unit.
Analysts expect NTT DoCoMo to list its shares by the middle of 1998.
Hironobu Sawake, an analyst at Nikko Securities, said: "NTT will avoid the listing this year because the fourth tranche sale of NTT shares by the Ministry of Finance is possible later this year."
NTT's cell phone unit is fast taking away sales from DDI Corp and other rivals on the strength of its strong brand name, attractive products and nationwide network.
